intro: The PTSD — Children 6 Years and Younger is a psychosocial scoring tool used in paediatric practice. DSM-5 preschool subtype criteria after exposure to actual/threatened death, serious injury or sexual violence. It scores 16 criteria and interprets the total across 2 bands, so the number always arrives with the severity it implies rather than on its own. In PediAid each criterion is shown as a labelled option with the weight it carries, so the total can be checked rather than taken on trust.
indications: Grading severity at the bedside in psychosocial
Recording an objective severity band in the case notes
Deciding when a total crosses the threshold for escalation
Re-scoring to track whether a child is improving or deteriorating
Checking the exact criteria of a score used infrequently
method: The score sums 16 criteria: Recurrent involuntary intrusive distressing memories (may be expressed in play); Recurrent distressing dreams related to the event; Dissociative reactions / flashbacks (may be trauma-specific re-enactment in play); Intense or prolonged distress at exposure to reminders; Marked physiological reactions to reminders; Avoidance of activities, places or physical reminders; Avoidance of people, conversations or interpersonal situations that are reminders; Substantially increased frequency of negative emotional states (fear, guilt, sadness, shame, confusion); Markedly diminished interest or participation in significant activities, including play; Socially withdrawn behaviour; Persistent reduction in expression of positive emotions; Irritable behaviour and angry outbursts (including extreme tantrums); and 4 further criteria. Totals are then banded: any score - Below threshold: threshold not yet met - check the per-cluster minimums, not just the total; 3 criteria met or more - Threshold met: preschool PTSD needs ≥1 intrusion symptom (items 1-5), ≥1 avoidance OR negative-mood symptom (items 6-11), and ≥2 arousal symptoms (items 12-16), lasting >1 month.
guidelineRefs: DSM-5 threshold: 3 or more of the 16 criteria listed.
A diagnosis also requires clinically significant distress or impairment, the required duration, and exclusion of substance use or another condition. Screening aid only - not a diagnosis.

faqs.q: How many criteria does the PTSD — Children 6 Years and Younger use?
faqs.a: 16. They are Recurrent involuntary intrusive distressing memories (may be expressed in play); Recurrent distressing dreams related to the event; Dissociative reactions / flashbacks (may be trauma-specific re-enactment in play); Intense or prolonged distress at exposure to reminders; Marked physiological reactions to reminders; Avoidance of activities, places or physical reminders; and others.

faqs.q: What do the bands of the PTSD — Children 6 Years and Younger mean?
faqs.a: The total is interpreted as: any score - Below threshold: threshold not yet met - check the per-cluster minimums, not just the total; 3 criteria met or more - Threshold met: preschool PTSD needs ≥1 intrusion symptom (items 1-5), ≥1 avoidance OR negative-mood symptom (items 6-11), and ≥2 arousal symptoms (items 12-16), lasting >1 month.

faqs.q: Does the score replace clinical judgement?
faqs.a: No. It is a structured way to record and communicate severity. A clinician concerned about a child should act on that concern regardless of the total.

faqs.q: Where does this score come from?
faqs.a: DSM-5 threshold: 3 or more of the 16 criteria listed.
Yes. Score definitions are bundled with the PediAid app, so the score computes without a connection.
